request: In the watchlist, show movies I haven't watched yet before the ones I've watched.

requests.title: Watchlist > toggles watched when the checkbox is clicked
requests.reason: Kind: modification (nothing removed or weakened; one re-query re-targeted, one assertion added). Genuine conflict with the required unwatched-before-watched ordering: the current production code already meets every stated requirement — `movies` is a `Signal<WatchItem[]>` computed as `[...this.store.items()].sort((a, b) => Number(a.watched) - Number(b.watched))` (no map/clone, store objects returned), the `@for` already uses `track movie.id`, and the original `(change)`/row-click guard semantics are intact. The toggle happens exactly once, but after Movie 1 becomes watched its row correctly moves behind Movie 2's unwatched row (requirement 4), so the test's post-click `checkbox()` helper — which re-queries `.watchlist-item` index 0 — returns Movie 2's unchecked checkbox and the unchanged test fails with 'expected false to be true'. No production change can make the unchanged test pass, because row index 0 is by definition a different movie once rows reorder at runtime. Minimal intent-preserving fix: capture the clicked checkbox node before the click (`const box = checkbox(); box.click();`) and assert `box.checked` on that same node after the reorder, plus assert it is still labelled 'Watched: Movie 1' (same DOM row stays bound to the same movie, per requirement 4). The `watchedCount()` and subtitle assertions are byte-identical.

requests.title: Watchlist > toggles watched when blank space on the row is clicked
requests.reason: Kind: modification (nothing removed or weakened; the index-0 re-query re-targeted to the captured node, one assertion added). Same root cause as the checkbox test: clicking blank space on Movie 1's row toggles it exactly once (the `closest('a, button, input')` guard is unchanged), but the row then correctly moves into the watched group, so the unchanged test's post-click `checkbox()` query hits row index 0 — now Movie 2's unchecked checkbox — and fails with 'expected false to be true'. This is a latent index-coupling in the test that the required runtime reordering exposes, not a code regression. Minimal intent-preserving fix: capture the row and its checkbox before the click and assert on the captured checkbox afterwards, plus `expect(items()[1]).toBe(row)` to pin requirement 4 — the very same DOM row moves to the watched group while remaining bound to the same movie. All other tests are untouched.
